chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The camel hirer and the cameleer who travels and has no fixed residence should complete the prayer (four rak'ahs) and fast the month of Ramadan (fully, without shortening).

key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: The cameleer; one who owns and manages camels for transport
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: The hirer of camels; one who hires camels for transport
key_terms.يَخْتَلِفُ: He travels/moves from place to place
key_terms.يُتِمُّ الصَّلَاةَ: He completes the prayer (performing four rak'ahs instead of two)

ai.seo_question: Do traveling merchants with no fixed home need to shorten their prayers and fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of itinerant workers like cameleers who, despite constant movement, lack a fixed domicile (muqim), thereby obligating them to perform full prayers (salat al-tamam) and fast completely. This ruling distinguishes them from typical travelers who are permitted to shorten prayers, highlighting the Shia juristic principle that the absence of a stable residence negates the concession of travel. The narration underscores the importance of residential stability in determining religious obligations, a key concept in Usuli fiqh.
